own_solution.law: Thin-rod longitudinal wave speed v_rod = sqrt(E/rho); free-free fundamental (clamped at middle) lambda_rod = 2L, f = v_rod/(2L); in air lambda_air = v_air/f; node spacing = lambda_air/2 = L v_air/v_rod
assumptions: thin rod (diameter << wavelength), no lateral-inertia correction
fundamental free-free mode with node at the clamp
air column resonates at rod frequency
dust heaps at displacement nodes, spaced half a wavelength

notes: v_rod = sqrt(7.0e10/2700) = 5091.75 m/s; f = 5091.75/2.4 = 2121.6 Hz; lambda_air = 0.16167 m; spacing 0.08084 m (8.08 cm). With the rod lengthened to 1.52 m before clamping (clamp at the new middle): spacing = 1.52*343/5091.75 = 0.10239 m. Cross-section/diameter: area enters both stiffness EA and mass per length rho A and cancels in v = sqrt(E/rho); a K label (thin-rod regime, 8.2-14 mm diameter << 2.4 m wavelength) would also be defensible. Note that 8.21 mm diameter gives 0.529 cm^2, not 1.6 cm^2, but the diameter and area sentences are never added together, so no contradiction arises. TFBD6/T2604 lengthen the bar on the rack, not the rod: disconnected; the clause 'before the clamp is fitted' attached to the bar reads a little oddly but the rod/bar distinction is explicit in the base text. TA297/TFE55 apply only to an earlier run.
